payload.body: Make native host plugins/MCP the authoritative control plane for h2a across Claude, Codex, Antigravity (agy), Hermes, and OpenCode. The server owns drumbeat and wake delivery; agent skills are plugin-first; harness hooks deny direct h2a CLI execution when the native plugin is available, with a break-glass path only when it is unavailable. Replace client-side nohup/watch/tick and direct CLI spawning with plugin tool calls and server-issued wake envelopes. Add cross-host conformance tests and explicit host capability/fallback matrix.
payload.title: WP: Native-plugin control plane — wake, launch, and CLI harness guard

payload.statement: When a native h2a plugin/MCP server is live for the host, the server—not a skill or shell process—owns scheduling, liveness, and wake delivery; no client-side h2a loop watch/tick/nohup process is started.

A loop emits a wake only for a deduplicated actionable state transition addressed to a live target (for example completed builder, unresolved blocker, failed required review, or explicit human gate); it never wakes a conductor merely because refs are absent, a presence is stale, or a periodic poll occurred.

Claude, Codex, agy, Hermes, and OpenCode harness adapters deny direct h2a CLI launch, delegate, watch, tick, wake-request, conductor-launch, and other mutating/supervisory commands while their native plugin is available; plugin tools remain the normal path and a logged break-glass fallback is permitted only when native plugin health is unavailable.
Agent launch and relay use native plugin tools and durable server envelopes; they do not rely on tmux send-keys, client polling, or a skill executing h2a CLI.

Cross-host conformance tests cover capability detection, CLI denial, break-glass fallback, wake deduplication/coalescing, actionable-transition gating, and no wake storm under idle/no-ref/stale-presence conditions.

A created loop with enrolled live participants is scheduled server-side durably: its policy tickMs is honored without a conductor shell, foreground watch, client poll, or manual tick. A dry-run/noop observation cannot be mistaken for an active drumbeat; scheduler state and next-run/last-transition are surfaced by the plugin.

The loop engine executes already-authorized, reversible, in-scope steps autonomously (observe, delegate through plugin, test, review, report, retry within policy, and advance declared dependencies). It asks a human only at an explicit decision boundary: irreversible/public effect, scope or authority expansion, sensitive access/cost, competing valid objectives, unresolved conflict, or an ambiguity material to outcome.

Host plugins render a compact actionable wake and allow approve-all for the loop authorization class; they do not emit one confirmation request per ordinary operation or require a user message to resume a created loop after an idle/noop tick.

Mandatory end-to-end acceptance scenario (run for every supported host: Claude, Codex, agy, Hermes, OpenCode): (1) create a disposable objective loop exclusively through the host native plugin/MCP tool—no h2a CLI process and no pre-existing shell watcher; (2) assert plugin/server reports durable drumbeat armed with tickMs and observable next-run; (3) leave an enrolled disposable participant pending/idle, advance controlled test time or wait one tick, and assert the server emits exactly one deduplicated plugin wake/relaunch envelope according to policy; (4) let the participant complete one ordinary in-scope reversible step, then assert it advances/reports without any per-operation h2a confirmation. Capture durable server events, host-plugin receipt, and participant result as evidence.

The E2E loop receipt fails if loop creation came from CLI or a client watcher; if a drumbeat is dry-run-only, unscheduled, silent past tickMs, duplicated, or routed through tmux/send-keys; or if the host prompts for confirmation for creation, ordinary in-scope delegation/retry/test/report, or wake handling. The test explicitly permits human confirmation only at the documented irreversible/sensitive/out-of-scope decision gates.
Rendered managed tmux status bar identifies the actual canonical h2a session and never emits stale remote-h20 placeholder/legacy label when a managed session is known.
Rendered status surface shows active managed subagents, gateway health/state, selected/configured model/value, and explicit unavailable/error states rather than omitting them silently.

Automated rendering tests cover canonical local and remote names, stale legacy fallback suppression, zero/multiple subagents, gateway available/unavailable, and configured versus effective model values.

La porte de test du depot est aveugle sur pres du tiers du code, et c'est la porte qui est REQUISE sur main depuis le 2026-07-26 avec enforce_admins.

Mesure du 2026-07-29 sur un clone neuf a l'historique complet :

  scripts/run-tests.mjs
    NODE_TEST_DIRS  = packages/h2a/test, packages/focus-interactive/test
    VITEST_SUITES   = packages/track

  Ce qui tourne     : 1654 tests node + 1142 tests track = 2796
  Ce qui ne tourne PAS :
    packages/h2a-runtime             73 fichiers, 1138 tests
    packages/remote-k8s-orchestrator  4 fichiers
    packages/remote-protocol          3 fichiers

h2a-runtime porte le lanceur de sessions, le proxy du gateway, le catalogue de modeles et le maillage LLM — soit exactement le code ou les defauts de la semaine ont ete trouves (bac a sable codex non configure, modele injoignable accepte, prompt non delivre a la lane). Ses 1138 tests n'ont jamais garde une seule PR.

Consequence directe : tout enonce « npm test vert » emis dans ce depot, y compris ceux de la CI et ceux que j'ai rapportes moi-meme toute la journee du 28-29/07, est plus etroit qu'il n'en a l'air. Le chiffre est vrai ; sa portee ne l'est pas. C'est une assurance fabriquee par une absence.

Cette absence etait deja soupconnee (note « CI ne lance pas les tests du runtime ») ; elle est desormais mesuree.

A faire, dans cet ordre :
- ajouter packages/h2a-runtime a VITEST_SUITES (ou au bon runner selon son harness) et faire tourner la suite ;
- traiter les echecs que ce premier passage revelera — il y en aura, personne ne les a vus depuis des semaines ;
- ajouter remote-k8s-orchestrator et remote-protocol ;
- ajouter un test structurel qui echoue si un paquet contenant des *.test.ts n'est couvert par aucune entree du runner. Sans lui, le prochain paquet ajoute retombera dans le meme trou en silence.

Le dernier point est le seul qui empeche la recidive : les trois premiers corrigent l'etat, le quatrieme corrige la cause.

payload.body:
La numerotation des WP compte les conteneurs annules. Un WP annule garde sa position dans la serie, et le WP suivant herite du numero d'apres — pas du numero libere.

Mesure du 2026-07-29 : apres annulation de quatre conteneurs (WP14 a WP17), un WP cree ensuite recoit WP18 alors que 14 a 17 ne designent plus rien de vivant. La serie rendue devient WP1..WP13 puis WP18.

Contournement applique : assigner un code explicite (item assign-code --code WP14). Il fonctionne parce que 14 n'etait pas reserve par un code stocke, seulement occupe positionnellement. Ce contournement echoue des qu'un code a ete assigne a un conteneur ensuite annule — le code reste pris a vie, l'erreur etant "code already assigned to container, codes are roster-global unique".

Deux defauts distincts, a traiter ensemble :
- la derivation positionnelle compte les annules ;
- un code assigne n'est jamais libere, meme quand son porteur est annule, et rien ne permet de le reassigner ni de retirer le role d'un conteneur (set-role n'accepte que workpackage|stream).

Consequence pour l'owner : la serie des WP se troue a chaque restructuration, et le seul recours est une chirurgie sur les evenements. C'est ce qui a ete fait aujourd'hui, apres avoir annule a tort deux WP qui correspondaient exactement au besoin.

Lie a la decision du 2026-07-29 : un item clos sans validation humaine doit pouvoir etre rouvert. Rouvrir resoudrait aussi ce cas — un WP annule par erreur redeviendrait vivant sans toucher aux evenements.

PRINCIPE : tout ce qui possede un WP est un acteur durable, porteur d'une memoire. Quatre acteurs sont transverses, sept portent un domaine. L'owner a tranche CONDUCTOR, en citant le precedent de ses autres projets, avec l'avis de l'architecte comme contre-poids. La separation se fait par l'avis, pas par la propriete.
Ce desaccord est consigne pour qu'un conflit futur sur l'autorite du conducteur soit relu a la lumiere de ce qui avait ete signale.

Owner, 2026-07-29 : le remote control doit etre actif sur toutes les sessions lancees.

Mesure du meme jour : impossible aujourd'hui.

  h2a run claude <ws> --name rcprobe claude --remote-control rcprobe
  -> error: unknown option '--remote-control'

`run` valide ses options et refuse celles qu'il ne connait pas ; il n'y a donc ni drapeau propre, ni passage vers la CLI hote. Aucune session lancee par h2a ne peut avoir le remote control.

Or le depot en depend deja. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-31-evo1-bilateral-discussion-driver-framing.md` decrit le pilote de canal natif comme rendant `claude --remote-control <name> --brief -p ...` « quand le nom de remote-control est present ». Ce nom n'est jamais present, puisque rien ne le pose : le chemin natif ne peut donc jamais etre choisi, et `auto` retombe systematiquement sur local-tmux. C'est un garde qui ne peut pas se declencher — la capacite est decrite, jamais atteignable.

A livrer :
- une option de lancement qui pose le nom de remote-control, par defaut egale au --name de la session pour que l'agent soit adressable sous un seul nom ;
- l'activer par defaut sur les sessions claude, l'owner l'ayant demandee pour toutes ;
- verifier que le pilote de canal natif l'emprunte reellement une fois le nom present, plutot que de continuer a retomber sur tmux ;
- consequence attendue : piloter une session sans passer par tmux, ce qui est le prerequis du remote control via sentropic (item ouvert WP12).

A verifier avant de coder : quelles autres CLI hotes ont un equivalent (codex expose `app-server` et un daemon `remote-control`), pour que l'option ne soit pas claude-only.

MEASURED 2026-07-29 in packages/track:
  state/fold.ts sets `body` ONLY from item.created and decision.created - no other event touches it.
  cli/index.ts reads --body ONLY inside `item new`.
  ingest/contract.ts accepts `body` ONLY on item.create and decision.create.
So a body is WRITE-ONCE at creation, with no amendment verb and no amendment trace.

LIVE INSTANCE, the same evening: cond (WP4) recorded in the body of 01KYR0B3GHESME1KF2H6CAP8E5 the conclusion that "an actor who honestly traces a blockage penalises itself in the table" - an inverted incentive at the heart of the steering instrument. Measured here as FALSE (the second row is a blockage, prefixed thr:, and the WP rollup counts one item). cond retracted it explicitly at 23:16Z and could not amend the body: their own words, "le corps de l'item n'est pas editable (journal append-only), donc la conclusion fausse y reste ecrite".

CONSEQUENCE: a reader who opens that item tomorrow reads the retracted conclusion as fact. The retraction lives in an h2a message (ephemeral) and in a sibling item's body (01KYQZVQY5CYK3DEDTST4S36R6) that nothing links to it. A journal whose statements cannot be corrected in place, and whose corrections are not reachable FROM the wrong statement, produces confident wrong reading - the exact class of failure the 2026-07-29 reopening ruling addressed for realization.

NOTE THE FAMILY, all three measured tonight: (1) a closure could not be corrected -> fixed, PR #83; (2) a closure records no motive -> traced, 01KYQZVR72MR3NWM2V0ZTR7SW8; (3) a recorded FACT cannot be corrected -> this item. Same defect class on three axes.

Append-only is NOT the obstacle: a correction is one more event, exactly like the reopening. Design direction to instruct: an additive body-amendment event carrying the new text plus a reason, folded last-write-wins, with the superseded text kept in the log (the trace IS the value, as in spec.amended). Decide whether the correction is authored-by-anyone or restricted, and whether the report shows "corrected" the way it should show "reopened".

Found by the harness lane on 2026-07-29 while acting on the independent review of the test gate.

MEASURED, same commit, same lib, same code:
  packages/h2a-runtime/src/conv-guard-wiring.test.ts launched from packages/h2a-runtime : 17 failures
  the same file launched from the repository root                                       : 12 failures

CAUSE. Five of these tests compute their expected slug by REIMPLEMENTING the product rule on process.cwd() - basically cwd.split("/").pop(). The package directory is itself named h2a-runtime, which the product legitimately parses as the managed session name h2a- + runtime. So the naive reimplementation and the product disagree, but only when the launch directory happens to look like a managed name.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THESE FIVE. A suite whose result depends on the basename of the checkout directory is the same family of landmine as a test pinned to an absolute clock: it is green or red for a reason that has nothing to do with the code, and it is green for most people most of the time. Concretely it already produced two exact-but-different failure counts in two independent reviews of the same branch on the same evening, which cost a round of reconciliation.

CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY MEASUREMENT OF THIS REPOSITORY. A failure count for this suite is meaningless without stating where it was run from. The root test runner launches Vitest from each package directory, so the root gate sees the 17-failure form.

SHAPE OF THE FIX, for the owning lane. A test must not reimplement the rule it is testing. These five should call the product helper that derives a slug, or pin an explicit cwd fixture instead of inheriting process.cwd(). Fixing them also removes the dependence of the gate number on the runner cwd.

NOT REPAIRED HERE: the harness lane does not implement the lanes it guards, and these are behaviour-bearing tests of session launch.

payload.body:
Measured by portal (WP12) on 768 events, re-measured here on 795, and sharpened - the defect is worse than "the journal cannot attribute a write".

THE MEASUREMENT, whole journal, zero exceptions:
  by            -> human:fabien.antoine@m4x.org   795/795
  prov.auth     -> local-user                     795/795
  prov.principal-> ABSENT                         795/795
  transport     -> cli 708, import 87

THE MECHANISM, read in cli/index.ts:224-246 (not inferred):
  cliActor() derives `by` from `git config user.email`. Twelve lanes share one checkout and one git identity, so they all write as the owner.
  CLI_PROV is the constant {transport:'cli', proposed:false, auth:'local-user'} - `principal`, the field the contract defines for "the verified-principal identity the channel attests", is never populated by anyone.

WHY THIS IS THE HARD VERSION: the comment above CLI_PROV states the log "honestly distinguishes a human-CLI write from an agent one". It cannot. An autonomous agent running the CLI is recorded with proposed:false and by=the owner's email - the journal says A HUMAN DECIDED when an agent did. That is a guarantee stated wider than its evidence, written in a code comment, in this package. On the enforceability ladder it is worse than a missing field: it is a field that reads as an assurance.

CONSEQUENCES MEASURED TONIGHT, both real, both by other lanes:
  portal could not learn who reparented an item inside its own WP - the answer came by h2a message, never from the registry.
  an item (01KYQXJX3PRWY5TT4SEN3W8KD1) was reparented out of WP8 and cancelled 150 ms later, and no one can say by whom.
  the RACI being reviewed in PR #84 attributes accountability for ACTS; a registry that cannot attribute an act cannot make a RACI violation detectable, so a RACI rule is a habit, not a guarantee.

THE SPLIT, because half of this is not mine: the WHO must come from the ingest CONTEXT (D3 design - track records, it never verifies), so h2a must supply a per-lane identity (prov.principal + proposed:true for an agent write). What is MINE: the CLI must be able to accept and record it instead of hard-coding a human constant, and the read surfaces must expose/filter it. Also mine, and cheap: stop claiming in a comment a distinction the code does not make.

DO NOT "fix" this by inventing an actor name a caller can assert freely - a name that anybody can write attributes nothing (same trap as h2a's unverified actor field). Recording an ATTESTED principal, or recording nothing and saying so, are both honest; a self-declared name is not.

payload.body:
MEASURED tonight, on a live instance that damaged real work.

.track/events.jsonl and .track/head.json are COMMITTED files (git ls-files .track). So every git worktree carries the journal AS OF ITS COMMIT. Measured on two checkouts of this repo, at the same moment:
  worktree at origin/main : 667 events
  repository root (writer): 797 events
An agent working in a worktree therefore reads a journal 130 events behind, and NOTHING says so.

THE FAILURE IS SILENT AND IT LOOKS LIKE ABSENCE, NOT STALENESS:
  in the worktree, `track item show 01KYQXJG77DQC368F4G2B2VGD8` returns `null`, exit 0.
That item exists - it is the very mandate the agent was sent to implement, traced at 21:48Z tonight. My subcontractor could not read its own mandate and correctly reported "returned null in this isolated worktree"; a less careful agent reads `null` as "this item does not exist" and invents a scope.

The whole delegation flow of this project points into this trap: the shared-tree rule says deliver from an isolated worktree based on origin/main, and doing exactly that makes the delegated agent blind to everything traced since that commit - including its own mandate and every decision that arbitrates it.

WHAT IS NOT THE DEFECT: the single-writer rule. Writing from the root only is correct and must stay. This is about READING.

Expected, in order of increasing cost: (1) a read against a store whose head is behind the repository HEAD says so instead of answering `null` - staleness and absence must not be the same output; (2) a documented, one-flag way for a worktree agent to read the writer's journal (TRACK_DIR / --track-dir exist, nothing tells an agent to use them); (3) decide whether a committed journal snapshot should be readable by default at all, given that every worktree makes one.
payload.title: An agent in a worktree silently reads a stale committed journal: item show returns null for real items

Expected: either honour 'required' for profiles that can use the gateway, or REFUSE the launch explicitly when 'required' is impossible for the requested profile. MEASURED 2026-07-29, same instance (claude:h2a:c18853e319ea), one evening:
  21:43Z  inbox readable inline
  22:35Z  h2a_inbox read returns 162 921 characters -> refused, over the token ceiling, spilled to a file

Each lane sends measured, substantive envelopes. The conductor is the single reader of all of them.   2. a subjects-only mode: id, sender, createdAt, subject, without bodies. A conductor triages on subjects and opens what matters.

I did not read the store implementation, I do not know whether a read filter is a one-line addition or a contract change, and I have not checked whether the MCP token ceiling or the tool itself is the binding constraint. Do not close this on my diagnosis - the numbers are mine, the design is coop and the protocol.

payload.body:
Diagnosed by the harness lane on 2026-07-30 from the CI log of PR 93. It is what makes the h2a-runtime suite hang in CI, and it is a product defect, not a test problem.

MEASURED, from the required job log (build-and-test ubuntu-latest node 20; identical on node 22):

  "[h2a] connection lost - reconnecting..."   3 982 276 lines
  "[h2a] reconnected"                          3 982 275 lines
  window: 2026-07-29T23:56:43.5 -> 2026-07-30T00:06:40.7

That is roughly 6 670 cycles per SECOND for the entire ten-minute cap, ending only when the runner SIGKILLs the suite. Not a burst: the full window.

THE MECHANISM, readable in the code rather than inferred. packages/h2a-runtime/src/attach.ts, around lines 299-330. The outer loop reads the events stream; when the stream ends it writes "connection lost", then enters a retry loop of up to 120 attempts. On FAILURE it waits 1000 ms before the next attempt. On SUCCESS it sets the reader, writes "reconnected" and BREAKS - with no delay at all. Control returns to the outer loop, which reads the new stream. If that stream also ends immediately, the cycle repeats with ZERO delay, unbounded. The 1000 ms guard protects the failure path only; nothing paces the succeed-then-immediately-lose path.

WHY THIS IS A PRODUCT DEFECT AND NOT A CI ARTEFACT. In production the same shape applies: a control-plane that answers 200 with an event stream that closes at once makes `h2a attach` spin at thousands of reconnects per second, flooding stderr and burning a core, with no backoff and no ceiling on the cycle itself (the 120-attempt cap is per outage, and a successful reconnect resets it). A caller sees an attach that appears alive and consumes a CPU.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and I will not guess it. Why the reopened stream ends immediately in CI while the same suite finishes in about two seconds locally. Three lines of "TypeError: Body is unusable: Body has already been read" appear just before the cycling starts, which is consistent with a Response body being consumed twice, but that is a lead. The trigger is unidentified; the mechanism above is not.

CREDIT WHERE IT IS DUE. The cyber lane eliminated the two-core-runner hypothesis by measurement (--maxWorkers=2 locally: no hang) and was the first to point at this reconnection path, while explicitly refusing to call it the cause because the retry loop it had read is bounded. That refusal was correct AND the path was the right one: the bounded loop is the failure path; the unbounded one is the success path, and only the CI log shows it.

SHAPE OF THE FIX, for the owning lane: pace or bound the succeed-then-lose cycle, not just the retry. A minimum interval between successive stream opens, or a cap on reconnections per unit time, would turn a livelock into a clean failure.

CONSEQUENCE: the test gate (PR 93) cannot be installed until this stops hanging the required check.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is a governance one: the owner cannot distinguish HIS OWN merges from those of twelve autonomous agents. Neither in `gh pr view`, nor in the merge commit author, nor in the branch protection audit trail. Every merge on this repo is attributable to exactly one human who did not necessarily perform it. So the rule the owner set - never a merge without a test AND two review legs - has no audit surface: he cannot check after the fact whether it was honoured, and he cannot tell which merges were his.

SECOND FACT, and it is why this matters now rather than later: PR 85 was merged on ONE independent leg plus a green gate, not two legs. plugins states it plainly and does not hide it. It was docs-only, and the owner did say on 2026-07-28 that one review can suffice when the first pass was already high quality - so this is not established as a breach. What IS established is that nobody could have told, because the merge carries no actor.

  presence does not carry the launch name, so a subcontractor cannot be attributed to its lane (01KYR5EFZV7M45GZV8QNM7RZQP, WP2)
  all 856 journal events carry the same `by`, so no track event can be attributed to an actor
  and now: no git merge can be attributed to an actor
Three surfaces, one absence: there is no actor identity that survives into any record this project relies on. arch wrote that an identity is proven by possession and not by a name; here there is neither.

DIRECTION, not a specification: the question is not "how do we sign a merge" but "which surface should carry the actor, once, so that all three inherit it". That is an identity question, hence this WP, and it is arch own act to place. A per-surface patch would give three conventions that drift.

I did not check whether a per-lane GitHub App or a commit trailer is available in this setup, and I have NOT established that any merge other than PR 85 was performed by a lane - PR 85 is the only one measured. index.ts:4997-5020 refuses to restart an active session, and is meant to TELL the user when that session runs without the current llm-mesh env. Measured 2026-07-30 on origin/main af9e8e4c.

registryEntryForResumeTarget (index.ts:2005-2016) applies parseManagedSessionName to its target. That target serves TWO different things: a session name typed by a human (h2a resume h2a-myproject), and a slug DERIVED from the current directory when no name is given. De-prefixing is right for the first and wrong for the second.

Consequence: any working directory named h2a-<x> or remote-<x> is silently reinterpreted. Measured from packages/h2a-runtime, the product computes the slug "runtime" where the directory is "h2a-runtime", then looks for a session that does not exist. Five conv-guard-wiring expectations in the "h2a resume <slug>" block fail only when the suite runs from that directory, and pass from the repository root - the harness lane established that by comparing failing SETS with the launch directory as the only variable.

The expectations are RIGHT: a directory called h2a-runtime is a directory, not a managed session name. I first repeated the harness lane classification of this as a test-design defect and withdrew it: the test reimplements the slug rule, but its reimplementation is EQUIVALENT to the product one (both basename plus the same substitutions) - I compared them. The disagreement comes from the de-prefixing, which only the product does.

FORM OF THE FIX: distinguish the two uses instead of overloading one string - an explicitly-named target may be parsed as a managed name, a slug derived from cwd may not. Not attempted here: it belongs to the resume path and should not travel as a passenger in a restore branch.

SIDE NOTE worth keeping: this also means any measurement of this suite depends on the NAME of the checkout directory. A test suite whose result varies with its checkout basename is the same family as one pinned to an absolute clock.

MEASURED INCOHERENCES, all present on the owner machine on 2026-07-29 and none detected by any tooling: (1) two codex marketplaces pointing at deleted tmp/deploy-* build dirs, which made codex plugin marketplace list fail outright and blocked listing/installing/upgrading EVERY codex plugin, h2a included; (2) the codex plugin running from a frozen 0.85.18 cache while the npm CLI was 0.88.0 - a version skew between the npm package and the host plugin that nothing compares; (3) two equally dead directory marketplaces still configured in Claude, silently tolerated because the canonical git-sourced one happened to work; (4) orphan plugin cache directories left behind by removals. EXPECTED: a single idempotent command (natural home: extend h2a doctor, which already does root split-brain/hygiene/prune) that DETECTS and REPAIRS host installation incoherence for claude and codex - dead marketplace source, plugin/npm version skew, duplicate or stale marketplace entries, orphan caches, missing or double h2a MCP endpoint - reports what it changed, and is safe to re-run. Fail-closed on anything it cannot repair, never a silent partial. ACCEPTANCE is an owner UAT on a deliberately broken installation, not a green suite. ROUNDS 5 TO 8, recorded together. ROUND 5 (SHA 5cdf6ea8) NO-GO, and its first blocker is the most valuable finding of the PR because it would have broken a HEALTHY machine: packages/h2a/.codex-plugin/plugin.json declares mcpServers './.mcp.json' relative to the PLUGIN ROOT, while loadBearingArtifacts joined it to dirname(manifestPath) and therefore looked for .codex-plugin/.mcp.json - a phantom path. Probed against the exact shipped layout: a CLEAN installation exited 2 with a restart required on that non-existent path, permanently. The targeted fixtures did not carry the real mcpServers field, so 21/21 never saw it. A fixture that omits what the product ships is not a fixture. Second blocker: the declared set was incomplete - 12 SKILL.md actually loaded, 2 Claude hook files, the command='h2a' binary resolved through PATH and its startup import closure were uncompared, so a really-loaded skill modified after session start exited 0. DESIGN DECISION BY plugins, taken alone and reported to the conductor as a deliberate SCOPE REDUCTION so the owner can contest it: the reviewer recommended building the proof from the whole loaded graph; I REFUSED, because that road ends at 'everything the process might import' including a PATH-resolved binary, which is not knowable from the filesystem, and five rounds showed enumeration does not converge. ROUND 7 (de9c0cab) NO-GO on THE MOST DAMAGING DEFECT OF THE PR, and it was found inside a claim plugins had personally read the code for and vouched for: isLegacyH2aPlugin accepted /^h2a-local-/i OR /@sentropic-local-/i, and the SECOND alternative was NOT anchored on h2a, so a third-party selector such as openai@sentropic-local-fixture was classified as legacy H2A and repairClaude emitted 'claude plugin uninstall openai@sentropic-local-fixture'.
